s: A gaming company runs an Aurora PostgreSQL global database with a primary cluster in us-east-1 and secondary clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Applications connect through the global database writer endpoint. A Regional service event makes the us-east-1 cluster unreachable. Business leadership accepts losing a few seconds of recent writes but wants writes restored as quickly as possible, without manual connection-string changes, and with the remaining Regions still replicating afterward. What should the solutions architect do?
o: Run a global database switchover to us-west-2 so that the global writer endpoint is updated automatically.
Run a global database failover (allow data loss) to us-west-2. The writer endpoint follows the new primary, and eu-west-1 keeps replicating from it.
Detach the us-west-2 cluster from the global database, promote it to a standalone cluster, and update the application configuration with the new cluster endpoint.
Restore the latest automated snapshot of the us-east-1 cluster into us-west-2 and point a Route 53 CNAME record at the new cluster.

w.y: When the primary Region is unavailable, the managed failover (allow data loss) promotes a secondary, rebuilds the topology around it, and moves the global writer endpoint. That is exactly what 'accepts losing a few seconds' and 'without manual connection-string changes' ask for.

o.A: Switchover needs a healthy primary to synchronize with, so it is not the right operation during an outage.
o.B: Correct: managed failover gives a fast RTO, keeps the other secondaries attached, and the global writer endpoint moves with it.
o.C: Detach-and-promote needs manual connection changes and leaves eu-west-1 out of the topology.
o.D: A snapshot restore takes much longer and loses far more data than storage-level replication.

d: fastest write recovery, accept seconds of data loss, no config changes
